findingDetails.title: A refusal typed with the retired command name still delivers the live mutating command
findingDetails.scopeProof: command-attach.ts and handlers/advisor-recommend.ts are in the declared scorer-attach scope; the handler is the only production caller of typedCommandForTop.
findingDetails.claim: A refusal written with the retired command name still attaches the live command because the retired-name rewrite runs before the mention guard.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: The compiled route for the same prompt returns defer, so the typed path is the live caller; the probe confirms the top row is sk-doc.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The retired name could be treated as a distinct command, but the map's comment says it reads as the replacement, so the guards should agree.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if the retired name is deliberately excluded from the live command's refusal semantics.

findingDetails.title: A coordinated refusal names the second command without a lead, so the typed path still delivers it
findingDetails.scopeProof: The prompt is an ordinary refusal of two tracked commands; the typed path and handler are in scope, and no other module rewrites the lead.
findingDetails.claim: A refusal that coordinates two command names attaches the second one because the mention reader requires a separate lead before each occurrence.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: The compiled route returns defer and the scorer top is system-deep-loop; a single-command refusal is correctly withheld, so the gap is the coordinated form.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The reader may have refused only the first command and merely named the second, but 'do not run A or B' refuses both.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if a coordinated refusal is judged a mention of both commands rather than a refusal of both.

findingDetails.title: A correction inside one document still attaches the creation workflow when the sentence carries a generic creation word
findingDetails.scopeProof: All four prompts are correction requests inside an existing readme; the compiled route for the sk-doc hub and the attach function are the declared target.
findingDetails.claim: The small-edit gate treats generic creation words inside a correction clause as a request to create the whole document, so a correction prompt still receives /create:readme.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: The two REQ-004 control prompts return no command, and the phase Out of Scope excludes edits with no correction word; these prompts name a typo or grammar error.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: 'new' or 'make sure' could be read as a request to author a fresh document, but the sentence's verb is fix and the object is an existing readme.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if the creation-request guard is intentionally broad and these clauses are judged outside the correction class.
